short: The price a customer actually pays for one unit.
seoTitle: Selling Price — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Selling price is the amount a customer pays for one unit of a product or service. Selling price is where cost, competition and positioning meet.
definition: Selling price is the amount a customer pays for one unit of a product or service. Depending on the trade it may be quoted inclusive or exclusive of tax, and it is the denominator in every margin calculation.
bodyHtml:
Why Selling Price matters

Selling price is where cost, competition and positioning meet. Setting it from cost alone ignores what the market will bear; setting it from competitors alone ignores whether you can afford to sell at that price.

Selling Price formula

Selling price = Cost ÷ (1 − target margin as a decimal)

Using cost × (1 + markup) instead gives a price based on markup, which is a different number.

How Selling Price works in practice

Work out the price your target margin needs, compare it to the market, and treat any gap as information — either your costs are out of line or your positioning has to justify the difference.

faq.question: How do I price for a 40% margin?
faq.answer: Divide cost by 0.6. A ₹300 cost needs a ₹500 price.

faq.question: Should the selling price include GST?
faq.answer: For consumer-facing sales an inclusive price is usual; B2B quotes are typically exclusive.
